Embeddings / reranker

Prompt governance

Security

Thanks — Tom

Hi all — attaching a short bundle (sdk-auth-samples.zip) and embeddings-best-practices.md (see attachments list). High-level answers + snippets below. I will bring runnable snippets to Thursday’s call.

Auth patterns (examples)
- API key (short-lived recommended): send in Authorization header: 
  Authorization: Bearer <redwood_api_key>
- OAuth / OIDC: standard bearer tokens + token refresh with scopes (good for user-scoped access).
- mTLS: supported at the transport level; we can provision certs for Dedicated/Private deployments. Use mTLS for agent-facing production endpoints where possible.

SDK notes
- Our SDKs (Python/Node/Go) support config for auth providers and automatic retry/backoff. Examples included in sdk-auth-samples.zip.

Embeddings & rerank pattern
- Candidate gen: BM25 -> top 200 candidates.
- Dense re-rank: embed candidates and query with same embedding model; compute dot-product / cosine; then re-rank top 20 with a cross-encoder if you need semantic re-score (higher quality, higher latency).
- Latency: embedding call (small model) ~10-25ms/token depending on model/hardware; cross-encoder re-rank for top-20 at 50 qps requires batching and dedicated capacity — expect p99 end-to-end re-rank latency in the 80-200ms range on dedicated GPUs with our recommended config. We’ll provide perf numbers for your exact corpus on the call.

Structured output & tool calling
- We recommend explicit JSON schemas for any tool-calling output. Example (simplified):
  {"action": "CHECK_PRICE", "params": {"product_id": "string"}}
- Use server-side validation of returned JSON against the schema (don’t trust the model).
- Limit allowed actions via an allowlist and verify auth when the system invokes internal APIs.

I’ll upload the sample bundle to the shared Drive by EOD.

— Dev
Senior SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi team — a few recommended patterns to cover routing, prompt governance, and red-team approach before Thursday.

Routing & model policies
- Policy engine: define rules like "if latency_target <= 50ms route to q4_8bit_lowlat; else route to base_high_quality". We can attach confidence-based routing: if model confidence < threshold, escalate to higher-quality model.
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallback on OOM/errors; circuit-breaker for degraded hardware.

Prompt templates & versioning
- Store prompt templates in Git (or S3) with semantic version tags and a checksum for each deployed version.
- Use an immutable artifact (prompt_id + version) in the request metadata so inference logs map to the exact prompt version.
- Enforce PR review / sign-off for changes to system prompts; tie changes to CI that runs unit tests (sample prompts + eval harness).

Prompt injection mitigations / red teaming
- Strong system prompt guards: explicit instructions, deny-list tokens, and explicit separators.
- Input sanitization: strip or encode embedded instructions, enforce token budgets for user input appended to system prompts.
- Runtime checks: detect anomalous instructions via a lightweight classifier and block or escalate.
- Red-team plan: periodic adversarial prompt generation, run against staging and compare outputs vs golden set; flag regressions and require ticketed remediation.

Structured output enforcement
- Always validate returned JSON against schema server-side. Reject or sandbox unexpected actions. Keep tool allowlist minimal.

I’ll attach a short prompt_governance_1.0.pdf with the above patterns and a checklist we can run during PoC.

— Vivek
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
